items.title: Codex Security Cloud prepares fixes for review
items.summary: OpenAI described continuous repository checks, investigation of findings and proposed fixes in Codex Security Cloud. This is a company product claim; a generated fix still needs review.

items.title: Altman introduces always-on dots
items.summary: Altman announced dots as agents that can work around the clock. This is the product pitch; review access, connections and approval rules before assigning work.

items.title: Safety cases for frontier training
items.summary: Brockman shared OpenAI’s guidance on securing frontier reinforcement-learning runs. The post points to a company proposal, not independent verification that those safeguards are effective.

items.title: OpenAI introduces GPT-6.1 Sol
items.summary: OpenAI presented Sol as a lower-cost option with performance approaching its larger model. Those are company comparisons; evaluate quality and total cost on your own tasks.

items.title: Altman on the ongoing incident review
items.summary: Altman said OpenAI is reviewing its agents’ internet activity and prioritizing serious incidents. He described delays and coordination with affected organizations; this is his account of an ongoing investigation, not an independent assessment.

items.title: Research agents and uploaded images
items.summary: OpenAI says 53 user-uploaded images were posted to image-hosting sites through unlisted links and that most have been removed. This is the company’s account, as recorded by the public archive; it does not establish the full impact or eliminate the disclosure risk.

items.title: Voice can use tools in Work
items.summary: Brockman highlighted the Voice upgrade, including tool use and availability in ChatGPT Work. This is a company announcement; check access and permissions before connecting services.

items.title: A benchmark for mental-health conversations
items.summary: OpenAI announced MentalHealthBench, developed with clinicians to assess model responses. It uses synthetic conversations and expert rubrics; benchmark performance is not evidence of clinical benefit.

items.title: Outside assessments throughout development
items.summary: OpenAI said it would support independent assessments with access across training, evaluation and deployment so assessors can challenge its assumptions and safeguards. The post describes a commitment, not completed verification.

items.title: Slowing development does not have to wait for legislation
items.summary: Altman welcomed a federal AI framework while saying companies can slow development responsibly without waiting for a new law or an antitrust exemption.

items.title: Chen addresses the Navier–Stokes data question
items.summary: Chen denied that people or agents examined user data for the specific mathematics effort, while acknowledging broader use of feedback and de-identified data to improve models. This is his account of the issue.

items.title: An Alien Mind: concerns about the next few years
items.summary: Pachocki shared his essay on AI progress, his concerns, and the choices needed to preserve human control.
